$comment: Cross-language `flatten` conformance corpus. GENERATED by scripts/generate-flatten-corpus.py from the Python oracle - do not hand-edit. Each case pins the canonical FlattenedSystem field set of esm-libraries-spec §4.7.5 step 4 for one shared fixture: the ordered contents of every map, the per-variable metadata (units, default, shape, update kinds, distribution kind, and the bounds `lb` / `ub`: null when absent, the number, or the flattened reference - esm-libraries-spec §4.7.5, "Bounds follow the renaming"), every equation, and the derived system_kind. ORDER IS PART OF THE CONTRACT - a parameter vector is positional, so a binding that sorts or uses map-iteration order is non-conforming. The parameter subsets brownian_parameters / discrete_parameters PARTITION `parameters` (esm-spec §6.3.1); they are recorded as name lists because their full metadata is already in `parameters`, where each MUST also appear. `state_variables` and `observed_variables` are NOT a partition: `state_variables` is the solved-for vector and `observed_variables` is the §6.3.1 classification, so an ARRAYED observed - one an indexed LHS defines, which materializes into a buffer rather than being inlined - appears in BOTH, carrying the role `observed` in each (issue #270). Each equation's `contributions` is its per-term provenance (esm-libraries-spec §4.7.5): the ordered summands whose LEFT-FOLD sum is the right-hand side (the `faq` body for a pointwise-lifted equation), each carrying its origins, `{"component": <dotted path>}` or `{"coupling": <0-based index into the coupling sequence after coupling_import expansion>}`. Compared exactly and in order. A pointwise-lifted state (a key of `lifted_shapes`) carries the lift's index sets as its `shape`, and its lifted `faq` ranges read `{"from": <index set>}` (esm-libraries-spec §4.7.5, "Pointwise lift: index sets"). Every expression (an equation side, a summand, an event condition or affect side, a bound or default that is an expression, a field initial condition) is as `canonicalize_document` writes it (API_SPEC §5.4) and compares as a JSON value with every number in its canonical kind (§5.5.3.1). Entries in `refusals` must be rejected, with the named error type.

refusals.reason: Chem declares its own `ic(c)` and the operator's `ic(_var)` template expands onto `Chem.c` as well, so `Chem.c` has two initial conditions. esm-libraries-spec §4.7.5 step 4: `field_ics` holds at most one entry per state, so flatten refuses rather than let one silently win.

the pointwise lift needs the synthetic index set `_liftdim1_3` (two declared index sets have size 3 and no shaped operand chooses between them), but the document declares `_liftdim1_3` with size 4. esm-libraries-spec §4.7.5, "Pointwise lift: index sets": every name in a lifted state's shape is an index set of the dimension's extent, so flatten refuses rather than shadow the declared set.

`Box.x` reads the [lev] `Column.T` and `Box.y` reads the [lat] `Column.S`, so the two lift candidates would put the one component `Box` on two different grids. esm-spec §10.5 and esm-libraries-spec §4.7.5, "Pointwise lift: which states are lifted": the unit of lifting is the whole component, so flatten refuses rather than choose a grid.

`Box.x` reads the [lev, lat] `Column.TS`, so `Box` is lifted onto [lev, lat] in the first pass; `Box.y` reads `Other.z`, which that pass lifts onto [lev], so `Box.y` is a candidate on [lev] only once `Box` is already lifted. esm-libraries-spec §4.7.5, "Pointwise lift: which states are lifted": all of a component's candidates must name the same index sets, whichever pass sees them, so flatten refuses rather than broadcast `Box.y` along lat.

`Box` is lifted onto [lev] by `Box.x` in the first pass; `Box.y` reads `Other.z`, which that pass lifts onto [lat], so `Box.y` is a candidate on [lat] once `Box` is already lifted. esm-libraries-spec §4.7.5, "Pointwise lift: which states are lifted": the same two-grids refusal as when both candidates are seen in one pass.

a pure template LIBRARY: templates and no component. There is nothing to flatten, and a library file must stay generic (its metaparameters bind per import edge), so flatten refuses rather than instantiating it at its defaults.

a `couple` connector applies `multiplicative` to `Surface.resistance`, a constant parameter with no `D(...)` tendency. esm-spec §10.3 and libraries §4.7.2 both define the transform against the target's EXISTING ODE RHS, so there is nothing to multiply. Four of five bindings used to drop the connector equation SILENTLY -- the document declared a coupling and the flattened system carried no trace of it. This case exists so `couple_multiplicative_no_tendency` cannot rot the way `operator_compose` did: every fixture that used the idiom was migrated to the §10.4 `variable_map` spelling, which left the diagnostic with no fixture at all. It lives in tests/coupling/ and NOT in tests/invalid/ because it is schema-valid and structurally valid -- `tests/invalid/` means `validate()` must reject, and this document is refused at FLATTEN. Same placement rule as valid/template_import_lib.esm.

EDGE CASE 10 of this catalogue maps `SingleVariableSystem.x` onto `EmptySystem.nonexistent_param`, which the document declares nowhere. Every binding used to flatten it CLEANLY with the entry silently dropped: the substitution runs over a name nothing references and the promotion pops a key that is not there, so the flattened system is indistinguishable from one where the coupling applied and happened to have no effect. That is the failure mode issue #198 item 1 reports from the other end -- a target that keeps its declared default, and (when it is the SOURCE that resolves to nothing) consumers rewritten to a name no table binds, which reads NaN at run time rather than raising. Same placement rule as `couple_multiplicative_no_tendency`: schema-valid and structurally valid, refused at FLATTEN, so it lives in tests/coupling/ and not tests/invalid/.

the data-fed `Met.K` declares `shape: []` and the `param_to_var` target `Box.F_k` is shaped [rec, x], so the rewritten equation reads `Met.K[1, i]`. esm-libraries-spec §4.7.3: the source survives with its own declaration, and `[]` declares a scalar buffer; only a source that declares NO shape takes the target's, so flatten refuses instead of reshaping it.

one data-fed source `Met.K[rec, x]` feeds `Box.F_k[rec, x]` and `Box.G_k[x]`. A source that declares a shape keeps it (esm-libraries-spec §4.7.3), so the edge onto `Box.G_k` is refused whichever coupling entry comes first.

the data-fed `Met.K` declares no shape and feeds `Box.F_k[rec, x]` and `Box.G_k[x]`. A shapeless source takes the shape of the targets it replaces (esm-libraries-spec §4.7.3), so they must all declare the same one; otherwise the shape it gets would depend on coupling order.

rejected at LOAD with rewrite_rule_nonterminating (esm-spec §9.6.3), so it never reaches step 4. Recorded so a binding that reaches flatten with this document knows its rewrite fixpoint is wrong, not its flatten.

uncovered_tiers.reason: ConflictingDerivativeError (step 4's pre-flight over-determination check) has no fixture FILE in tests/: every binding builds the conflicting document inline in its own suite. A shared fixture would be worth adding, and this corpus would then pin the refusal.
